claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Adding 1–2 at.% Al to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will promote formation of an Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
At approximately 1000 °C in air, the added Al will segregate to the alloy surface.
Surface-segregated Al will rapidly oxidize into alumina.
The resulting alumina scale will be continuous, adherent, and slow-growing.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the alumina scale will prevent further oxidation of the bulk alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will have lower oxide-scale growth than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for 100 hours.
The Al-modified alloy will have lower oxidation-associated weight gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for 100 hours.
Limiting the Al content to 1–2 at.% will preserve the alloy's intrinsic bulk microstructure.
The 1–2 at.% Al-modified alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The 1–2 at.% Al-modified alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The stated conditions imply high-temperature exposure under mechanical loading at specified strain rates, whereas the experiment exposes samples first and performs tensile tests only post-exposure. Thus, simultaneous oxidation-and-loading behavior is claimed but not tested.
